title: Elon Musk: The Man Who Bet Everything

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2008, this man had three failed rockets, a car company running out of cash, and money for maybe one more try.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2026, he became the first trillionaire in human history.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That's not a typo. A trillion. With a T.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: His name is Elon Musk. Some people call him a genius. Some call him a walking meme. Honestly? Probably both.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But the wildest part of his story isn't the money. It's how close he came to losing all of it. Hold that thought. We'll get there.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: This is the story of Elon Musk.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Pretoria, South Africa. June 28th, 1971. Elon Reeve Musk is born.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: As a kid, he reads everything. When he runs out of books, he reads the encyclopedia. For fun.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At school he's small, nerdy and badly bullied. One attack puts him in hospital.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So he escapes into computers. At twelve, he writes a space shooter game called Blastar, and sells it to a magazine for five hundred dollars.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Twelve years old, and already selling space stuff. Some things never change.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At seventeen, he leaves for Canada with very little money. Later he moves to the United States and studies physics and economics.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 1995, he starts a PhD at Stanford. He lasts two days.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two days. Some people take longer than that to return a pair of shoes.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Because the internet is exploding, and Elon wants in.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: With his brother Kimbal, he starts Zip2, an online city guide with maps, built for newspapers.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Money is so tight, Elon sleeps in the office and showers at the local YMCA.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then in 1999, computer giant Compaq buys Zip2 for 307 million dollars. Elon's share is 22 million. He's twenty-seven.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So naturally, he buys a million-dollar McLaren F1 supercar. A few months later, he crashes it. It wasn't insured.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Lesson one from Elon Musk: go fast. Lesson two: maybe get insurance.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: His next idea is bigger: X.com, an online bank. It merges with a rival startup and turns into a little thing called PayPal.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2000, while he's on a plane to Australia, the board quietly replaces him as CEO.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Still, in 2002, eBay buys PayPal for one point five billion dollars. Elon walks away with around 180 million.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Most people would retire to a beach. Elon decides to build rockets.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Why rockets? Because he wants humans to live on Mars. And when he checks the price of a rocket, the answer is: a lot.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So he flies to Russia to buy old missiles. The meetings go badly. It turns out, can I get a discount on your missiles, is a tough opening line.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: On the flight home, he decides to build his own. In 2002, he founds SpaceX.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Experts give it almost no chance. Because rocket science is, well, rocket science.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Falcon 1, flight one. 2006. It crashes.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Flight two. 2007. It fails.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Flight three. August 2008. It fails again.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And now, SpaceX has money for one more launch. Maybe.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Meanwhile, his other big bet is also on fire. Back in 2004, Elon put millions into a small electric car startup called Tesla.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Its first car, the Roadster, is fast and beautiful, and costs far more to build than anyone planned.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then the 2008 financial crisis hits. Tesla is running out of cash. Elon takes over as CEO and pours in almost everything he has left.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That same year, his marriage ends. He later called 2008 the worst year of his life.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Remember when I said he came close to losing everything? This is the moment.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: September 28th, 2008. Falcon 1, flight four. The last shot.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And this time, it reaches orbit. The first privately developed liquid fuel rocket ever to do it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then, days before Christmas, NASA gives SpaceX a 1.6 billion dollar contract to fly cargo to the space station.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Elon's reaction? Three words. I love NASA.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And on Christmas Eve, at the last possible moment, Tesla's emergency funding comes through.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two companies, both saved in the same week. Santa was clearly a fan.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: From here, things move fast. In 2010, Tesla goes public. In 2012, SpaceX's Dragon becomes the first commercial spacecraft to visit the International Space Station.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then Tesla's Model S arrives, and suddenly electric cars are cool.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: December 21st, 2015. A Falcon 9 booster flies to space, comes back, and lands standing up. A rocket that parks itself.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2018, the Falcon Heavy launches with a strange payload: Elon's own cherry red Tesla Roadster, with a dummy astronaut called Starman in the driver's seat.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: On the car's screen, two words: Don't Panic. It's still out there, circling the Sun. The most expensive way ever to avoid traffic.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And in 2020, SpaceX becomes the first private company to fly astronauts to the space station.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But Elon's biggest launches aren't always rockets. Sometimes, they're tweets.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2018, he tweets that he might take Tesla private at 420 dollars a share. Funding secured.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It wasn't. Regulators fined him and Tesla 20 million dollars each, and he had to step down as chairman.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The most expensive tweet in history. At least, until later.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then his tunnel company sells 20,000 flamethrowers. Officially named: Not a Flamethrower.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2019, he unveils the Cybertruck, with unbreakable armor glass. His designer throws a metal ball at it. The window smashes. On stage. Twice.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Elon's verdict? Room for improvement.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2020, his son is born. The name? X Æ A-12. Yes, really.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And in January 2021, he becomes the richest person on Earth for the first time.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Which brings us to the most expensive impulse buy in history.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2022, Elon offers 44 billion dollars for Twitter. Then he tries to back out. Then he buys it anyway.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Just before the deal closes, he walks into Twitter headquarters carrying a sink. His caption: let that sink in.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He fires most of the staff, sells the blue check marks, and in 2023 renames the whole thing: X.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Goodbye, blue bird. Hello, letter X. His favourite letter, in case you hadn't noticed.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2025, he goes to Washington to lead a government cost-cutting team called DOGE. It makes him a hero to some and a villain to others. A few months later, he's out.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Meanwhile in Texas, SpaceX is building the biggest rocket ever made: Starship.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Its first flight, in 2023, ends in an explosion. SpaceX calls it a rapid unscheduled disassembly.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Which is engineer language for: it blew up.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But in October 2024, the giant booster flies back to its launch tower, and the tower catches it with two metal arms. Fans call them the chopsticks.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Catching a skyscraper-sized rocket with chopsticks. Most of us can't even catch noodles.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then 2026 goes into overdrive. In February, SpaceX merges with Elon's AI company, xAI.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: On June 12th, SpaceX goes public. It raises 75 billion dollars, the biggest stock market debut in history.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: By the end of day one, SpaceX is worth more than 2 trillion dollars. And Forbes says Elon is now worth about 1.1 trillion.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Remember that guy with three failed rockets? Yeah. Him.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In September, Starship reaches orbit for the first time. Next up: catch both halves of the rocket. Then the Moon. Then Mars.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So who is Elon Musk, really?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A kid who sold a space game for five hundred dollars. A man who bet everything and nearly lost it all. A billionaire who posts like a teenager at 2 a.m.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Love him or hate him, he changed how we drive, how rockets fly, and how the internet argues.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And if your plan ever feels too crazy, remember: this whole story started with a guy trying to buy missiles from Russia.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: This was Unfiled Films. Is Elon Musk a genius, or just incredibly lucky? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for more stories like this.
